sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Republic of Panama) — Unitary National Jurisdiction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition) supplemented by codified commercial law, specialized offshore private interest foundation legislation, and regulatory practice derived from financial-action-task-force standards; judicial precedent is persuasive rather than strictly binding
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), in force 31 October 2012
Panama–Netherlands Double Taxation Agreement, in force December 2011
Panama–United Arab Emirates Double Taxation Agreement
Panama–Republic of Korea Double Taxation Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT Law), as amended by Ley No. 254 de 28 de octubre de 2021 establishing the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF), administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Decreto Ejecutivo No. 363 de 27 de julio de 2015 (resident agent licensing, client due diligence, and UBO reporting duties); Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Ley de Fundaciones de Interés Privado); Ley No. 70 de 2019 and applicable Código Fiscal provisions (annual foundation tax); binding directives of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) on terrorism financing and sanctions implementation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of founder's passport or national identity document (individual founder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority, civil registry, or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization at the Panamanian Consulate if the country of origin is not party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or extract of the commercial register (for juridical founder entities)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate or certificate of no criminal record for the ultimate natural-person founder, foundation council members, and beneficiaries
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or judicial authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter and source-of-funds / source-of-wealth declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution holding the founder's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and apostilled (or consular legalized) where required by the originating institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish sworn translation of all foreign-language public documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn public translator registered in Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before a Panamanian Notary Public (translated documents do not require separate apostille once notarized in Panama)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Acceptance letter of the Panamanian resident agent (carta de aceptación del agente residente) with confirmation of the registered office address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian resident agent (licensed attorney or law firm)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft constitutional charter of the foundation (proyecto de escritura constitutiva) including UBO disclosure schedule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before a Panamanian Notary Public and subsequent authorization by the Ministry of Government (Ministerio de Gobierno)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP classification and enhanced due diligence (EDD) for politically exposed persons, family members, and close associates under Ley No. 23 de 2015 as amended by Ley No. 254 de 2021; mandatory real-time screening of the founder, foundation council members, protector, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panamanian UAF domestic designations; any positive sanctions match requires immediate suspension of client onboarding and a suspicious transaction report to the UAF; standard due diligence is permissible for the Low_Risk_Standard online cosmetics retail scope, but UBO identification remains obligatory regardless of transaction size; AML/KYC records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the client relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — electronic name availability module ('Vistas y Certificados de Nombre') available at https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa; foundation constitutional charters are subsequently routed through the Ministry of Government (Ministerio de Gobierno) for official foundation authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet in Spanish; foreign-language expressions, including the English denomination 'Private Interest Foundation' or the abbreviation 'PIF', are permitted when rendered in Latin script and reflected in the constitutional charter; the name must incorporate 'Fundación de Interés Privado', 'F.I.P.', or 'PIF' and must be clearly distinguishable from all existing legal persons, registered trademarks, and official government entities without phonetic or visual confusion
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the requester may file a written administrative appeal (recurso de reconsideración y apelación) within five working days of notification before the Dirección General del Registro Público de Panamá; final judicial recourse lies with the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia; to avoid delay, a revised application may be immediately resubmitted with a new distinctive token, and the original name reservation may be reactivated within the statutory 30-day window by re-filing the official name request before the Registro Público.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted. The Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must maintain a licensed resident agent in Panama whose office address serves as the registered office; no physical branch, retail store, warehouse, or employees are required in Panama for the online cosmetics retail scope. All foundation administration may be conducted abroad by the foundation council. Physical importation or on-island sale of cosmetics into Panama would trigger Ministry of Health (MINSA) sanitary notification and registration, which is an operational compliance obligation separate from the registered office mandate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection is not more than 5% per foundation-year; inspections, when conducted, are directed to the resident agent's premises for verification of KYC and UBO files under Ley No. 23 de 2015 and Ley No. 254 de 2021, and do not extend to foreign operational facilities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability certificate (vista) at the Registro Público de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registral tariff for issuance of the name availability certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the foundation constitutional charter and issuing counsel's legal opinion under Ley No. 25 de 1995
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard Private Interest Foundation charter (USD 450–1,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ministry of Government foundation authorization filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official ministerial processing tariff for Private Interest Foundation authorization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry inscription of the foundation charter (protocolización e inscripción)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registral tariff based on charter value and number of folios, plus notarial protocolization fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent first-year service (registered office, compliance mailbox, regulatory notifications, UBO filing facilitation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian resident agent (licensed attorney or law firm)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Decreto Ejecutivo No. 363 de 2015 compliance; typical first-year range USD 450–650

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille of founder and UBO document bundle in country of origin (set of 3–5 public documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the country of origin (e.g., Secretary of State, Foreign Ministry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille tariff of the originating jurisdiction (varies by origin country)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation and notarization of apostilled or foreign-language documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn public translator and Panamanian Notary Public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff plus prevailing market rate for certified legal translation per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial ownership register (RUBF) filing for the foundation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) via resident agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Handling fee for electronic RUBF submission under Ley No. 254 de 2021

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, and EU sanctions screening and AML compliance file setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual market benchmark for low-risk individual screening (USD 100–150)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Annual foundation tax (Ley No. 70 de 2019, amend. Código Fiscal) — first-year payment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — payable via resident agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory annual flat fee for Private Interest Foundations (USD 400 per current Código Fiscal tariff)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory minimum foundation endowment (Ley No. 25 de 1995, minimum capital of USD 10,000 in cash or in-kind assets)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foundation estate (private declaration in the charter; no government deposit or custody)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum capital requirement — not a government fee; declaratory only, subject to the founder's contribution obligation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law No. 42 of 2017; Articles 5, 6, 8, 9-16, 17-24 and 33-34; Executive Decree No. 32 of 26 February 2001 (Regulations of Law 25); Unified Rules and Procedures of the Public Registry (Resolucion No. 201-2487 of 17 October 2017); supplementary application of the Panamanian Civil Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Publico de Panama (Public Registry of Panama), Private Interest Foundations Section (Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado), Calle 35 y 36, Arco Iris, Panama City, Republic of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Fundacion (Private Foundation Charter), formalized as a notarized private instrument and registered by inscription in the Special Registry of Private Interest Foundations; optionally supplemented by Reglamento (Foundation Regulations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum initial endowment of USD 10,000 (or equivalent in another currency) under Article 8 of Law No. 25 of 1995. No escrow account or paid-up bank deposit is required for registration; the endowment may be contributed in cash or in kind and is evidenced solely by the Founder's declaration in the Foundation Charter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL. Acting pursuant to Law No. 25 of 1995, the undersigned Council members hereby RESOLVE: (1) To accept the initial endowment of USD 10,000 in satisfaction of Article 8, no escrow deposit being required; (2) To ratify the Foundation Charter and fix the registered office in Panama City at the Resident Agent's office; (3) To confirm the Council and appoint [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary and [Name] as Treasurer; (4) To authorize bank and payment-processor accounts and e-commerce platform agreements; (5) To ratify all preparatory acts of the Founder. Adopted unanimously in Panama City.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama, online consultation platform Registr@ and Client Services Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform an availability search in the Public Registry database for the proposed foundation name, which must end with 'Fundacion de Interes Privado' or an acceptable abbreviation. File the name reservation request electronically through Registr@ or in person, pay the applicable search/reservation fee, and secure a 30-day reservation certificate before drafting the charter.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Copy of founder's passport or corporate identification documents
Proof of payment of reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or conflicts with an existing legal person name, resubmit with alternative denominators or distinctive words; an adverse refusal by the registry can be appealed administratively under the Unified Rules of the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Circuit (Notaria Publica del Circuito), Panama City.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct licensed Panamanian counsel to draft the Foundation Charter containing the foundation name, purpose (online retail of cosmetics and personal care products), endowment of USD 10,000, Foundation Council rules, beneficiary and Protector clauses, and registered office. The Founder and Resident Agent appear before the notary to authenticate the instrument; notarial fees are paid per the statutory tariff.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter and Regulations
Passport or corporate documents of the Founder
Resident Agent acceptance letter
Power of attorney if the Founder acts through counsel
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal or typographical defects, the draft is corrected and re-executed before the same or a different notary; no registry penalty attaches if resubmission occurs within the validity window of the reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration and Inscription at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Foundation Charter with the Private Interest Foundations Section, pay the registration rights computed on the declared endowment (base amount USD 250), and await the registry examiner's legal review. Upon approval, the foundation is inscribed in the Special Registry and acquires juridical personality; obtain certified copies, the inscription certificate, and a legal-person status certificate.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Foundation Charter for inscription
Certified Resident Agent acceptance
Receipt of payment of registration rights
Certificate of name reservation
Founder and Council identification records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'prevencion' (defect notice), respond with corrective documentation within 15 business days; if the inscription is refused, refile an amended instrument or appeal the registrar's decision under the Unified Rules of the Public Registry and Law 25 of 1995.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) with the National Revenue Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Publicos (ANIP), Registro Unico de Contribuyente, online portal and service offices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the foundation for the RUC (tax identification number) after inscription, elect the territorial-source tax regime applicable to Private Interest Foundations, and register the economic activity 'Retail sale via internet of cosmetics and personal care products' (ISIC 4791). Obtain the digital certificate and fiscal address record; no active tax status is granted until the registration file is completed.
required_dossiers: Certificate of inscription from the Public Registry
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
Resident Agent acceptance certificate
Fiscal address proof (written confirmation of the Resident Agent's office)
Identification of the Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any ANIP 'requerimiento' (information request) through the online portal within the stated deadline, supply the missing documents, and if the economic activity classification is disputed, file a clarification and request reclassification to ISIC 4791.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Operation Notice (Aviso de Operacion)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldia de Panama (Municipality of Panama), Direccion de Rentas Municipales.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operacion for the e-commerce retail activity, declaring the registered address (Resident Agent office, office, or warehouse) and the estimated municipal taxable basis. Pay the quarterly Industria y Comercio municipal tax, obtain the stamped aviso, and inscribe the foundation in the municipal taxpayer registry. Online-only retail is treated as a low-tariff commercial activity.
required_dossiers: RUC registration certificate
Foundation inscription certificate or certified copy of charter
Lease or ownership title of the premises
Completed Aviso de Operacion form
Beneficial ownership and due diligence declaration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality recalculates the tax or requires amendment of the activity description, submit a written reconsideration petition within 30 days and present the platform agreements proving internet-only sales; correct the payroll/activity data in the municipal register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Formalities and Onboarding of Financial Infrastructure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council and Resident Agent; supervised by the Public Registry and the Unidad de Analisis Financiero (Panama FIU) for AML/CFT compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizing session of the Foundation Council, adopt Resolution No. 1, open the statutory books (minutes book, resolutions book, members register), procure the foundation seal, and issue certified incumbency letters. Prepare the enhanced KYC file for opening bank, Shopify Payments, and PayPal accounts in the foundation's name, and appoint the compliance officer responsible for the customer due-diligence obligations under Cabinet Decree No. 14 of 4 February 2015.
required_dossiers: First Foundation Council Resolution (Resolution No. 1)
Certificate of incumbency for the appointed officers
Registered Agent certificate of good standing
KYC forms and identification of Council members, Protector, and ultimate beneficial owner
Statutory books opened and stamped by the Public Registry
Foundation seal certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or payment processor requests additional beneficial ownership records, update the foundation's internal beneficial ownership register and resubmit the KYC package; engage counsel to issue a legal-opinion consolidation letter describing the foundation's ownership and control structure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not triggered for ISIC 4791 online retail; sectoral reference only: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA), Direccion Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas, Cosmetics Notification Section, and Alcaldia de Panama for municipal licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No entity-level industrial or operational license is required for pure online retail of cosmetics. Conditional product-level 'Notificacion Sanitaria de Producto Cosmetico' (Cosmetic Product Sanitary Notification) under Executive Decree No. 381 of 12 July 2007 applies only if imported cosmetics are sold for physical distribution and consumption within the Republic of Panama.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Direccion de Evaluacion de Impacto Ambiental, Panama City, Republic of Panama.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Registration/Declaration of Low Environmental Impact) only if a fulfillment warehouse or physical storage premises is established; a Full EIA Report (Category II/III) is not required. Pure online retail with no manufacturing, no process wastewater, and no emissions-generating equipment is treated as exempt from EIA filing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No VOC or industrial wastewater thresholds applicable absent cosmetics manufacturing. If a warehouse is operated, comply with MINSA Executive Decree No. 1 of 2001 maximum permissible limits for wastewater discharge to sewer or surface waters; solid waste handling per Law No. 7 of 2014 and MiAMBIENTE Resolucion AG-0357-2018; general COPANIT technical standards for domestic sewage from sanitary facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection and annual certification of any warehouse/office premises by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panama; municipal structural load and use-of-premises clearance (permiso de uso) from the municipality's engineering department; workplace health-and-safety registration with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) and immediate employer enrollment with the Caja de Seguro Social upon hiring the first employee, per Law No. 12 of 1995 and applicable MITRADEL regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Primary electronic portal: SERT (Sistema Electrónico de Recaudación Tributaria) at sert.mef.gob.pa. Customs and export declarations are processed through the Single Window for Foreign Trade (SICE) of the Aduana Nacional de Panamá.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Register the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) deed in the Registro Público de Panamá and formalize the foundation council with a resident legal representative. 2. Apply for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) through SERT by filing the foundation constitution deed, charter, council appointment, proof of registered address, and identification of the founder and council members. 3. Activate the electronic tax domicile (domicilio fiscal electrónico) and obtain credentials for the Facturación Electrónica profile. 4. For export operations, pre-register as an exporter in SICE and obtain the Aduana user code before the first shipment. Non-resident foreign entities deriving Panama-source income may obtain an RUC through a duly designated fiscal representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama operates a pure territorial income-tax system and does not provide US-style check-the-box pass-through elections or hybrid-mismatch elective rules. The PIF is by default a separately taxable juridical person. Available statutory elections include: (a) election to apply the simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS regime for businesses with annual gross revenue up to USD 75,000 under Ley 119 de 2024; (b) election to obtain ITBMS exemption certificates for export purchases, subject to DGI exporter authorization; and (c) charter-level allocation of foreign-source income to beneficiaries, which remains outside Panamanian taxation by virtue of territoriality.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), Panama's VAT-type consumption tax; governed by the Código Fiscal and Ley 119 de 2024, with the 2025 reform transitioning the system toward the IVA denomination.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold: every person engaged in taxable economic activity in Panama must register for ITBMS regardless of turnover. Ley 119 de 2024 creates an optional simplified small-taxpayer regime for businesses with annual gross receipts of USD 75,000 or less, with fixed quarterly ITBMS payments in lieu of full monthly declaration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) applies through the SERT platform. All registered taxpayers must issue XML-format e-invoices via SERT or an authorized e-invoicing service provider, and each invoice receives a unique DGI security code and must be transmitted to SERT for validation within one calendar day. Export transactions must be flagged with the Exportación transaction type and reference the corresponding SICE export declaration number. Panama does not operate continuous real-time fiscal stamping clearance equivalent to Mexico's CFDI, but SERT rejects non-compliant invoice batches and requires correction and resubmission within the declaration period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) tangible goods physically exported from Panamanian inventory to a foreign destination and (ii) services rendered for the exclusive use and benefit of non-residents abroad. For beauty cosmetics DTC online retail, sales qualify as zero-rated exports only when goods are shipped from Panama by international courier or freight and the shipment is declared in SICE. Sales fulfilled from foreign warehouses or third-country fulfillment centers are outside Panama's territorial ITBMS nexus and are neither subject to ITBMS nor eligible for export refunds, whereas deliveries to consumers within Panama attract the 9% ITBMS rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA) validated in the Panama SICE export system
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Panamanian bank evidencing credit of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI systematically cross-matches zero-rated export lines in ITBMS returns against SICE export declarations, transport documents, and bank remittance certificates. Unsubstantiated zero-ratings are reclassified as domestic taxable sales and clawed back with a 1.5% monthly surcharge and interest, plus administrative fines of up to 300% of the omitted tax for intentional evasion, statutory penalties of up to USD 50,000 under Ley 119 de 2024 for documentary non-compliance, suspension of exporter status and RUC cancellation, and criminal tax fraud exposure with imprisonment of up to 8 years where forged export documentation is used.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as banking and monetary regulatory supervisor; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent of the Republic. Panama has no independent central bank and no foreign exchange administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is fully dollarized (U.S. dollar is legal tender) and applies unrestricted convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no exchange control regime, no central bank approval requirement, and no distinction between resident and non-resident for FX purposes. Profit remittances, capital endowment repatriations, and trade settlements may be freely executed in U.S. dollars or any convertible currency. The only practical hurdles are banking AML/KYC due-diligence compliance, correspondent bank screening, and Panamanian tax reporting obligations on Panamanian-source income.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to surrender or repatriate export proceeds. E-commerce export receipts from cosmetics retail may be retained in USD or other currencies, held locally or offshore, and used freely for operating expenses, supplier settlements, and reinvestment.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium for operational collection clearing, Low for statutory capital escrow or foundation treasury. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Wise Business, Currencycloud) can provide multi-currency settlement and virtual IBAN-like clearing through reciprocal correspondent banks, but they are not licensed as Panamanian banks and cannot provide the foundation capital verification or legal certification required by a Panama Private Interest Foundation. Such EMIs are also heavily risk-averse to PIF structures and may require audited foundation records or decline onboarding without a local licensed agent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is generally permitted for low-risk Panamanian PIFs when the applicant submits certified copies of the foundation charter, current foundation certificate (Paz y Salvo or equivalent), notarized and apostilled passports of directors/council members, and a licensed Panamanian attorney's legal opinion. No statutory rule mandates physical appearance, but SBP-regulated banks retain risk-based discretion to require a video interview or in-person meeting for non-resident ultimate beneficial owners, high-risk jurisdictions, or unusual transaction structures. In practice, appointing a licensed resident agent with power of attorney materially improves onboarding certainty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF with opaque beneficial ownership structure or legacy bearer share arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified foundation charter and current foundation certificate; register of council members and beneficiaries; sworn declaration of beneficial ownership; foundation council resolution appointing the bank; notarized passport copies of all UBOs; reference letter from a licensed Panamanian attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds inconsistency relative to the e-commerce cosmetics transaction profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed financial statements for the preceding two years (if available); Shopify and PayPal sales dashboards; supplier contracts and purchase invoices; historical bank statements tracing revenue; written explanation for the initial capital endowment source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdiction mismatch or inbound wire from a sanctioned or high-risk third-country counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Correspondent bank approval memorandum; OFAC and EU/UN sanctions screening results; legal opinion on beneficial ownership; commercial invoice and shipping documents for cosmetics trade; confirmation that no counterparty appears on sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction velocity or high-volume outbound payments to beauty manufacturers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply chain documentation, purchase orders, packing lists, shipping records, Panamanian tax filings consistent with ISIC 4791 e-commerce retail, internal AML monitoring framework, and periodic independent compliance certification from a licensed accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Complete SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 cover if interbank only) from the overseas founder/shareholder to the PIF's U.S. dollar account at a Panamanian bank. In the payment narrative field, state 'Capital Endowment to Private Interest Foundation [Foundation Number]'. Provide the foundation charter, capital contribution resolution, and documented lawful source of funds to the receiving bank before the transfer. If the correspondent clearing network requires a purpose code, use a generic 'Capital Transfer (g2a)' code; amounts above the bank's internal CDD threshold may require a written declaration of lawful origin and will be held for enhanced due diligence. The Bank for International Settlements or U.S. clearing rules do not alter the Panamanian unrestricted currency regime, but failure to provide source-of-funds documentation is the primary cause of wire rejection or account freeze.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for cosmetics inventory and fulfillment costs use SWIFT MT103 single-credit transfers in USD through the Panamanian bank's U.S. correspondent clearing network (Fedwire/CHIPS). For supplier invoices denominated in KRW, CNY, EUR, or other convertible currencies, the bank executes an MT103 with an FX conversion leg. For high-value purchase orders with new beauty manufacturers, an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit (LC) is recommended. The settling bank requires commercial invoices, packing lists, air/sea waybills, certificates of origin, and, when applicable, inspection certificates; maintaining a compliant supply-chain file prevents AML-driven settlement delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards (USD/CNY, USD/KRW, USD/EUR) entered into with SBP-licensed banks or reputable offshore counterparties
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted currencies (USD/KRW, USD/CNY) through global correspondent banks for cash-flow hedging
FX swaps for short-term treasury management where supplier payables and customer receivables create temporary currency mismatches
Cross-currency swaps (USD into supplier currency) for long-term purchase contracts with manufacturing partners, subject to foundation council approval and documented hedging policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax (Annual Government Maintenance Tax under Law 25 of 1995)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Public Registry of Panama, remitted through the licensed Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the foundation's registry anniversary; standard agent compliance applies a calendar-year cut-off of 31 March for the annual renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge accrues monthly for each month or fraction after the due date; unremitted annual taxes restrict the issue of good-standing certificates and may lead to administrative strike-off of the registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-ownership confirmation required for AML compliance (confirmation of ultimate beneficial owners of the PIF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Analysis Unit of Panama (UAF) and the resident agent's AML file; not a public-registry filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the resident agent's compliance review date, and within 30 days after any transfer of a foundation interest or change in beneficiary or council member
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML penalties under Law 23/2015, including administrative fines up to USD 1,000,000 for serious non-production or false beneficial-ownership records; persistent failure also creates resident-agent resignation and strike-off risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Panama-source income tax return (Form 102) / informative zero return where the foundation has no Panama-source taxable activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) through the foundation's RUC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March after the close of the tax year for calendar-year foundations; extensions only when granted by the DGI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty plus monthly interest on any tax due; three consecutive unfiled years may trigger forced assessment, embargo, and registration suspension

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory external audit exists for a Panama Private Interest Foundation that merely holds assets or performs non-Panama-source online retail activity. A certified audit becomes required where the foundation engages in a licensed Panamanian financial or insurance activity, where the foundation's charter or by-laws require an audit, or where the DGI or a bank/counterparty imposes an audit as a condition of operations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS / IFRS for SMEs as adopted by the Panamanian Technical Accounting Commission and accepted by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); books must be maintained in Spanish or English and must permit territorial-source income determination.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation Council must deliver to the Resident Agent a certified schedule of current beneficiaries, council members, and protected persons at least once per calendar year and within 15 days after any change. The confidential beneficial-ownership records are kept at the registered office in Panama and are shown to the UAF, DGI, or Public Registry upon a valid request; transfers of foundation interests reflected in the private ledger do not require public registration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation charter and by-laws and any amendments
Minute book with council resolutions and decisions
Confidential register of beneficiaries and beneficial owners
Accounting records and underlying transactional documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700–1,500 per year for resident agent, registered office, and compliance letter support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–6,500 for a compact statutory or independent audit of an active retail foundation; voluntary review and full IFRS engagements vary with transaction volume
